$comment: Copy of the public learn pages, by topic (docs/plans/visit-story-v2-offers-design.md, section 1.9). General information only: it says what usually happens, never anything about one patient, and always defers to the dentist. 'art' picks the generic still (a tooth type and the stage steps of @aarogyam/app-kit/mouth-art; 'brushing' for everyday care). Each step's 'label' is drawn on the still. English only; reviewed by: pending (founder).
general_note: General information about this treatment, not about your visit. If your dentist gave you different advice, follow your dentist's advice.

root_canal.summary: A root canal saves a tooth whose inner soft part (the pulp) is inflamed or infected. It often takes more than one sitting.

steps.label: Clean
steps.text: The dentist numbs the tooth, opens a small hole in the top and cleans the canals inside the roots.

steps.label: Medicine
steps.text: Between sittings, a medicine may be placed inside and the tooth is closed with a temporary filling.

steps.label: Seal
steps.text: When the canals are clean, they are filled and sealed.

steps.label: Protect
steps.text: A back tooth usually needs a crown afterwards, because a treated tooth can break more easily.

expect: Some tenderness for a few days is common.
Avoid biting hard food on the tooth until the treatment is finished.
Keep every sitting, so the tooth does not get infected again.
call: swelling appears or pain gets worse

filling.summary: A filling repairs a tooth after decay is removed, so the tooth can be used normally again.

steps.label: Decay
steps.text: Decay makes a soft, weak area in the tooth.

steps.label: Clean
steps.text: The dentist removes the decay, usually after numbing the tooth.

steps.label: Fill
steps.text: The space is filled and shaped so you can bite comfortably.

expect: If you were numbed, avoid chewing until the numbness wears off.
Mild sensitivity to cold for a few days can happen.
Brushing twice a day and fewer sweet snacks help the filling last.
call: your bite feels high after a day
pain or sensitivity keeps getting worse

extraction.summary: A tooth is removed when it cannot be saved or is causing problems. The gap then heals over a few weeks.

steps.label: Remove
steps.text: The area is numbed and the tooth is gently loosened and taken out.

steps.label: Heal
steps.text: A blood clot forms in the socket. It protects the area while it heals.

expect: Do not spit hard, rinse forcefully or use a straw on the first day.
Eat soft, lukewarm food and chew on the other side.
Keep brushing the rest of your mouth, gently near the area.
call: pain or swelling gets worse after the second day

wisdom_extraction.summary: Wisdom teeth are the last teeth at the back. One may be removed when there is no room for it or it causes pain or infection.

steps.label: Position
steps.text: An X-ray shows how the tooth sits in the jaw.

steps.label: Remove
steps.text: The area is numbed and the tooth is removed, sometimes in pieces.

steps.label: Heal
steps.text: The area heals over the next few weeks.

expect: Swelling and stiffness for a few days are common.
Do not spit hard, rinse forcefully or use a straw on the first day.
Eat soft food and keep the area clean as your dentist advises.
call: pain, swelling or fever gets worse

crown.summary: A crown is a cap that covers a weak or broken tooth to protect it and restore its shape.

steps.label: Shape
steps.text: The tooth is shaped so the crown can fit over it. A temporary crown may be placed.

steps.label: Fit
steps.text: The final crown is fixed in place.

expect: With a temporary crown, avoid sticky and hard food on that side.
Clean around the crown at the gum line every day.
A crown lasts longer with regular check-ups.

scaling.summary: A cleaning removes hard deposits (tartar) that brushing cannot remove, so the gums can heal.

steps.label: Tartar
steps.text: Tartar builds up near the gums and can make them red and bleed.

steps.label: Clean
steps.text: The dentist removes the tartar and polishes the teeth.

expect: Gums may feel tender or bleed a little for a day or two.
Teeth can feel sensitive for a few days.
Brush twice a day and clean between your teeth to keep tartar away.
call: bleeding or sensitivity does not settle

implant.summary: An implant replaces a missing tooth with a small post in the jaw that holds a new crown.

steps.label: Post
steps.text: A small post is placed in the jaw. It joins with the bone over a few months.

steps.label: Connect
steps.text: A connector is fixed on top of the post.

steps.label: Crown
steps.text: The new crown is fixed on the connector.

expect: Some swelling and tenderness after placing the post are common.
Eat soft food on that side while it heals.
Clean around the implant every day, like a natural tooth.
call: the implant or crown feels loose

sealant.summary: A sealant is a thin protective coating on the grooves of back teeth, where decay often starts.

steps.label: Grooves
steps.text: Deep grooves on chewing surfaces trap food and germs.

steps.label: Seal
steps.text: The grooves are cleaned and coated. No numbing is needed.

expect: You can eat normally soon after.
Keep brushing twice a day with fluoride toothpaste.
Sealants are checked at regular visits and touched up if needed.
call: the coating feels rough or chipped

general_care.summary: Simple daily habits keep teeth and gums healthy between visits.

steps.label: Brush
steps.text: Brush twice a day for about two minutes with a soft brush and fluoride toothpaste.

steps.label: Between
steps.text: Clean between your teeth once a day with floss or small brushes.

steps.label: Check-up
steps.text: Visit your dentist for regular check-ups, even when nothing hurts.

expect: Fewer sweet snacks and drinks between meals help prevent decay.
Help young children brush until they can do it well themselves.
Replace your toothbrush every few months.
call: a tooth hurts or a gum swells
gums bleed often when you brush
